added_provisions.reason: Registration of Title Act, No. 21 of 1998, s.44(a) requires a notary attesting an instrument under that Act to satisfy himself of the identity of parties not known to him by reference to their official identity cards. It is in force from 1998 with no amendment events, so it was available in October 2021. It does not govern an ordinary deed of transfer under the Notaries Ordinance, but it falsifies the draft answer's unqualified statement that no identity-document route existed at the matter date, so it is added as a supporting provision and cited by CL-M050-Q01-012.

question_decisions.note: The identification reasoning is verified end to end: rule (9) first limb as at October 2021 (recovered verbatim from 31-2022 s.16(6)), the good-repute and declaration limb of rule (9), the two-witness minimum in rule (8) and the joint-signature requirement in rule (12). The question is downgraded because the gold answer prose, which the verifier may not rewrite, contains one rule statement that cannot be supported at the matter date (rule (20)(b)) and one temporal statement that is too broad (no identity-document route in 2021), and because repealed rule (10) was in force at the matter date with its text unrecoverable, which leaves the conclusion's exhaustive framing unchecked.

disagreements.researcher_position: The identity-document route (national identity card, passport bio-page, driving licence) was not available to a notary in October 2021.
disagreements.verifier_position: True for a deed attested under the Notaries Ordinance, but not without qualification: Registration of Title Act s.44(a), in force since 1998, already required identity of persons not known to the notary to be established by official identity cards for instruments under that Act.

temporal_issues: The corpus holds no pre-2022 edition of the Notaries Ordinance. The rule (9) first limb in force in October 2021 is recoverable, but only because 31-2022 s.16(6) quotes the words it removed; the reconstruction was re-checked and is sound. 17-1852/s4 (Deeds and Documents (Execution before Public Officers) Ordinance), unamended since 1852, carries the same formula (party 'known to ... or to at least two of the attesting witnesses thereto, who shall make a declaration to that effect'), which independently corroborates the reconstructed wording.

Rule (10) of section 31 was repealed by 6-2024 s.3(4), so it was in force in October 2021, and neither the amending Act nor the consolidated text reproduces it. A rule sitting immediately after the identification rule and in force at the matter date is unreadable, so no answer to 'under what circumstances can the notary attest' can be treated as exhaustive on this corpus.
Rule (20)(b) pre-2022 wording and Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 pre-2022 wording are both unrecoverable, as the researcher recorded in corpus_gaps.

Rules (8) and (12) were re-checked against every amending Act touching section 31 (20-1976 s.10, 47-2011 ss.2 and 3, 31-2022 s.16, 6-2024 s.3); none of them touches either rule, so the researcher's temporal notes hold.
missing_definitions_or_exceptions: Section 32 disapplies rules (20), (23) to (26) and part of rule (16) for certain instruments, and never rule (8), (9) or (12); the researcher's exclusion of it is correct.

Section 33 (no invalidity for non-compliance in a matter of form) is not in the map. It is not needed for a question about the circumstances of attestation, but a lawyer may want it noted, since it bears on the consequence of getting the identification wrong.
1-1907/s43 defines only 'Council of Legal Education', 'High Court Judge' and 'Registrar-General'; nothing the answer turns on is a defined term, so no definition is missing.
Registration of Title Act s.44 was the one alternative attestation regime the researcher missed; added as PROV-M050-901.
case_law_dependence: None. The circumstances are set out exhaustively in the rules of section 31, and the answer cites no case.
enrichment_issues: FACT-M050-Q01-004 and, to a lesser extent, FACT-M050-Q01-003 restate the statutory test almost word for word ('persons of settled reputation', 'willing to sign a declaration at the foot of the deed that they are well acquainted with ... and know his proper name, occupation and residence'). No statute name or section number is leaked, but the conditions of rule (9) are handed to the answerer as facts, so a model can reproduce the conclusion without knowing the rule. The facts should be restated in lay terms before this is used as a benchmark item.

The enriched background otherwise keeps the original legal issue intact: the executant is still unknown to the notary, one witness is known to him, and the outcome still turns on the two-witness limb.
